title: I Let the Pool Locker Wristband Catch the Lifeguard Who Used the Family Bay

parts.text: I paid a family locker at 6:12 p.m. and lifeguard Tasha's street bag was already in bay F4 with no public wristband. The locker card said: WRISTBAND OPENS. STAFF USES STAFF. NO STREET BAGS IN FAMILY. I was forty-two, parent, holding a paid band. Tasha shrugged from the stand. "Guards are family." I photographed the bag, the card, and my unpaid-looking LED. Then I logged a staff bag. At 6:20 aquatics asked why Tasha's street bag was on F4. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Aquatics can see a lifeguard's street bag in paid family bay F4.

social.video_title: The lifeguard stashed a street bag in the family locker — Part 1/2
social.description: Pool locker, a paid wristband, and a street bag in F4. I logged the staff bag. Would you have photographed the LED?

parts.text: Tasha called it a break until aquatics asked for the log. I printed the staff bag, the photo, and the card. The bag moved to staff. Tasha broke in staff and told guards breaks were always about optics. Optics is a word lifeguards use when a street bag exists. Locker policy now has a second line: GUARDS ARE NOT FAMILY BAYS. I keep F4. Tasha staffs. The locker room finally looks like wristbands, not a break room. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
